symbols.name: S
symbols.def: A finite set of object types, finite outcome alphabets, relation roles, and specified finite context maps.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: A graph over attributes and relational contexts allowed by \(S\).

symbols.name: Rsrc
symbols.def: The listed finite source skeletons and their acyclic ground graphs.

symbols.name: Psrc
symbols.type: finite list of rational probability tables
symbols.def: The fully observed source joint laws indexed by \(Rsrc\).

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: The target relational skeleton and its ground graph.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A fixed assignment to a subset of ground variables in \(rho\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: A fixed event in the postintervention variables of \(rho\).

symbols.name: Ictx
symbols.def: The canonical explicit table listing every source ground node and every event-consistent target assignment term, together with each participating node's type--context key, parent tuple, intervention status, target relevance under \(a\) and \(B\), and multiplicity in the truncated factorization.

symbols.name: K
symbols.type: finite dictionary of rational conditional rows
symbols.def: The target-relevant type--context rows recovered from positive-probability source parent contexts in \(Psrc\).

symbols.name: rstar
symbols.def: The unique target-relevant row absent from every source support.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: The success probability in the unsupported binary row \(rstar\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: The dense coefficient list obtained by replaying the truncated target factorization encoded by \(S\), \(G\), \(rho\), \(a\), \(B\), and \(Ictx\), after substituting \(K\) and the shared row \((1-q,q)\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: The degree of \(F\), with \(D=0\) for a constant polynomial.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: The bit length of the canonical explicit encoding of \(S\), \(G\), \(Rsrc\), \(Psrc\), \(rho\), \(a\), \(B\), \(Ictx\), and \(K\).

symbols.name: LF
symbols.def: The bit length of the dense rational coefficient list of \(F\).

symbols.name: Mone
symbols.def: The compatible one-unseen-row model class constructed in \(\text{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q(M)=P_M^{rho}(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))\).

symbols.name: Theta
symbols.def: The set of values of \(Q\) over \(Mone\).

symbols.name: Ccrit
symbols.def: The boundary points and feasible distinct real roots of \(F'\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The minimum value selected from \(F(Ccrit)\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: The maximum value selected from \(F(Ccrit)\).

symbols.name: qminus
symbols.def: A selected candidate satisfying \(F(qminus)=L\).

symbols.name: qplus
symbols.def: A selected candidate satisfying \(F(qplus)=U\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: The complete finite-noise type-level mechanisms and their induced node-level source and target groundings for the lower and upper endpoint candidates.
symbols.role: serialized causal witness input to the checker

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: A record in the fixed grammar of \(\text{def:certificate-grammar}\), including an injective canonical digest of the complete fixed instance and \(Z\).

symbols.name: Check
symbols.def: The skeptical rational-arithmetic checker constructed in \(\text{def:checker}\).

symbols.name: Mminus
symbols.def: The lower serialized common model decoded from \(Z\), using row \((1-qminus,qminus)\).

symbols.name: Mplus
symbols.def: The upper serialized common model decoded from \(Z\), using row \((1-qplus,qplus)\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled source scenes used to construct supported-row confidence boxes.

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: The width of a supplied tree decomposition of the intervened target ground graph.

symbols.name: eta0
symbols.type: finite vector of conditional probability rows
symbols.def: The population values of the supported row dictionary \(K\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The truncated target factorization as a polynomial in the supported-row vector and the shared unsupported coordinate, normalized so that \(F(q)=H(eta0,q)\).

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: The familywise error level for supported-row boxes.

symbols.name: Cn
symbols.def: The product of coordinate confidence boxes intersected with each categorical row simplex.

symbols.name: etahat
symbols.type: rational vector of conditional probability rows
symbols.def: A deterministic feasible point of \(Cn\), chosen by boxed-simplex projection when \(Cn\neq\varnothing\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: For each supported row \(r\), \(m_r\) is a certified upper bound on its labeled occurrences in the target grounding.

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.def: For row \(r\), \(\epsilon_r=\min\{1,\tfrac12\sum_y\max(|\ell_{r,y}-\widehat\eta_{r,y}|,|u_{r,y}-\widehat\eta_{r,y}|)\}\).

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: \(\delta=\min\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\}\).

symbols.name: Lhat
symbols.def: \(Lhat=\min_{q\in[0,1]}H(etahat,q)\).

symbols.name: Uhat
symbols.def: \(Uhat=\max_{q\in[0,1]}H(etahat,q)\).

symbols.name: Kn
symbols.def: \(Kn=[\max\{0,Lhat-\delta\},\min\{1,Uhat+\delta\}]\), with \(Kn=[0,1]\) when \(Cn=\varnothing\).

assumptions.condition: Every endogenous attribute and every specified relational context in \(S\) has a finite domain.
Every source ground graph in \(Rsrc\) and the target ground graph \(rho\) is acyclic.
Distinct ground endogenous variables receive mutually independent exogenous noise draws.
One conditional mechanism row is shared by every occurrence of the same type--context key across \(Rsrc\) and \(rho\).
The laws \(Psrc\) factorize according to their ground graphs and agree on each type--context conditional row across source occurrences whose parent-context events have positive probability.
The set of type--context rows reachable in the intervened target query whose parent context has zero probability at every source occurrence is exactly \(\{rstar\}\).

novel.justification: This is a transparent local support pattern realized by the N3 traffic car whose two-signal context is absent from source A; every other target-relevant row is transferred only from an actually positive source parent context.

assumptions.condition: The outcome alphabet of \(rstar\) is binary with row \((1-q,q)\) for \(q\in[0,1]\).

novel.justification: Binary braking and no-braking mechanisms are directly relevant to the traffic consumer and make the unsupported row a single interpretable probability without imposing smoothness or oracle information.

assumptions.condition: For each supported row represented in \(Cn\), the parent-context event of its prespecified representative source node has strictly positive probability under the corresponding law in \(Psrc\).

standard.name: Positive conditioning-event support for sampled conditional rows

assumptions.condition: The random rational polytope \(Cn\) satisfies \(\Pr(eta0\in Cn)\ge 1-\alpha\).

definitions.name: One-unseen-row compatible RSCM class
definitions.construction: \(Mone=\{M: M\text{ is a finite RSCM over }S\text{ and }G;\ M\text{ induces the source groundings }Rsrc\text{ and target grounding }rho\text{ encoded by }Ictx,\text{ has independent ground noises and type-shared mechanisms, reproduces }Psrc,\text{ uses the rows }K\text{ recovered from positive-probability source parent contexts, and has exactly one unrestricted target-relevant binary row at }rstar\}\).

definitions.name: Feasible endpoint candidate set
definitions.construction: \(Ccrit=\{0,1\}\cup\{x\in(0,1):F'(x)=0\}\), with repeated roots represented once by the square-free part of an integer clearing of \(F'\).

definitions.name: Relational endpoint certificate grammar
definitions.construction: \(Gamma\) is a tagged record containing an injective length-delimited digest of \(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z\); local grounding and context-incidence records; a replayable sequence of truncated-factorization additions and multiplications whose dense output is \(F\); cleared integer numerator and derivative gcd data; disjoint rational isolators and Sturm root counts for every member of \(Ccrit\); boundary records; candidate-to-value links certified by resultants and Sturm--Tarski signs; shared labels for equal values; selected records \((qminus,L)\) and \((qplus,U)\); sorted rational-versus-algebraic breakpoint comparisons; and exact source and target evaluation records for both serialized model groundings in \(Z\).

definitions.name: Skeptical certificate checker
definitions.construction: \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)\) first recomputes the injective canonical digest and rejects any mismatch. It then verifies the schema and graph references, the exhaustive lexicographic indexing of source nodes and event-consistent target assignments in \(Ictx\), acyclicity and target relevance, the exact positive parent-context cells used to recover \(K\), and the unique unsupported key \(rstar\). It replays the target truncated factorization gate by gate and requires its dense coefficient list to equal \(F\). It next checks square-free data, Sturm root counts, resultant membership, Sturm--Tarski signs, candidate exhaustiveness, value ordering, tie labels, and algebraic threshold order. Finally it decodes both groundings in \(Z\), verifies type sharing, nonnegative finite-noise masses, independent node copies, mechanism outputs, exact reproduction of every source table in \(Psrc\), and exact target values \(L\) and \(U\); it returns one exactly when every clause succeeds.

definitions.name: Finite breakpoint endpoint model
definitions.construction: For each type, collect \(0\), \(1\), and all cumulative probabilities in its rows recovered from positive source parent contexts; insert the selected optimizer \(qminus\) or \(qplus\) for the free binary row; sort distinct breakpoints; assign one noise atom to each adjacent interval with mass equal to its length; let the shared type mechanism output the category selected by any interior point; give distinct ground nodes independent copies of this type-level noise; and serialize in \(Z\) every source and target grounding dictated by \(Ictx\).

definitions.name: Occurrence-coupled confidence enclosure
definitions.construction: Choose rational \(etahat\in Cn\) when \(Cn\neq\varnothing\), compute \(epsilon\), \(delta=\min\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\}\), compute \([Lhat,Uhat]=H(etahat,[0,1])\), and return \(Kn=[\max\{0,Lhat-\delta\},\min\{1,Uhat+\delta\}]\); return \([0,1]\) when \(Cn=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Proof-carrying compilation handle
definitions.construction: Start from exact variable elimination along a supplied bounded-width tree decomposition of the acyclic target grounding, represent messages by fraction-free univariate arithmetic circuits that preserve every type--context key, and produce the dense \(F\), complete \(Ictx\), and local gate identities accepted by \(Check\) without exhaustive target-assignment expansion.

statements.statement: The positive source parent contexts specified by \(Ictx\), source compatibility, and type sharing uniquely recover every row in \(K\). Replaying the truncated factorization of \(S\), \(G\), \(rho\), \(a\), and \(B\) yields \(F\in\mathbb Q[q]\). For every \(M\in Mone\), there is one scalar \(q_M\in[0,1]\) such that \(Q(M)=F(q_M)\); conversely, substituting any shared row \((1-q_0,q_0)\) yields \(F(q_0)\). The degree \(D\) is at most the maximum number of target nodes that can use \(rstar\) in one assignment.
statements.justification: This isolates the single structural degree of freedom without untying its repeated relational occurrences.
statements.gap: Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give a general polynomial program; the diagonal one-row collapse for a type-shared relational mechanism is not stated there.
statements.consumer: It converts the unsupported N3 mechanism row into an explicit target polynomial that can be bounded rather than represented by one fitted RNCM value.

statements.statement: The compatible causal set is exactly \(Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U]\). If the complete procedure of Ejaz and Bareinboim returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) for this fixed query and \(F\) is nonconstant, then \([L,U]\) is a strict informative refinement of that nonidentification report because it gives every and only compatible values. If \(F\) is constant, then \(L=U\), so the result is point identification and agrees with their identified-case conclusion; the absence of \(rstar\) alone does not imply that their complete procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
statements.justification: The theorem reports the exact relational compatibility range and sharpens a failure report only on instances where the complete comparator procedure actually fails.
statements.gap: Ejaz and Bareinboim establish a complete identification procedure and neural extrema correctness but do not return the sharp compatible set when that procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
statements.consumer: Experiment 6.1 can accompany its N3 fitted point with the certified population range; for its documented clamped count query, the theorem reduces to the known logical range \([0,1]\).

statements.statement: The breakpoint construction yields \(Mminus,Mplus\in Mone\) satisfying every source table in \(Psrc\) and \(Q(Mminus)=L\), \(Q(Mplus)=U\). The record \(Z\) serializes their complete type-level mechanisms and every induced source and target grounding specified by \(Ictx\). For each type \(t\), the number of positive noise atoms is at most \(1+\sum_c(|\mathcal X_t|-1)\) over its explicit contexts. Across each endpoint model, all noise masses are rational except at most two masses, each affine in the selected algebraic optimizer.
statements.justification: Sharpness requires legal common relational SCMs, not only algebraic optimizers.
statements.gap: Canonical-SCM and causal-order results construct attaining SCMs in broader response-function classes; they do not preserve this type-shared independent-ground-noise representation with the stated atom and algebraic-mass bounds.
statements.consumer: The serialized models let an auditor replay both endpoint traffic worlds and verify that every source assignment is reproduced.

statements.statement: If \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)=1\), then the digest binds \(Gamma\) to that complete fixed instance and those serialized groundings; \(Ictx\) is the exact source and target incidence table; \(K\) consists exactly of the target-relevant rows recovered from positive source parent contexts; \(rstar\) is the unique unsupported target-relevant row; and replay of the target factorization yields \(F\). The root records enumerate every point in \(Ccrit\), every candidate-to-value link is correct, \(L=\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\), and \(U=\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\). Decoding \(Z\) yields \(Mminus,Mplus\in Mone\), exact reproduction of \(Psrc\), and \(Q(Mminus)=L\), \(Q(Mplus)=U\). These conclusions remain valid with repeated derivative roots, boundary critical points, equal candidate values, boundary ties, algebraic conjugates, and threshold coincidences.
statements.justification: Soundness turns an untrusted producer's output into an independently checkable causal claim.
statements.gap: Li, Passmore, and Paulson and Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle verify univariate formulas; neither composes those checks with relational factorization and source-compatible endpoint models.
statements.consumer: A rejected conjugate or omitted positive critical point cannot silently alter the reported N3 range.

statements.statement: For every canonically encoded fixed instance \(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K\) satisfying the model assumptions, let \(F\) be the dense polynomial obtained by replaying its target factorization. There exist serialized endpoint groundings \(Z\) and a certificate \(Gamma\) such that \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)=1\). The combined bit length of \(Z\) and \(Gamma\), and the checker's bit running time on the complete input and certificate, are bounded by one fixed polynomial in \(D+LF+T+1\). Each selected optimizer and endpoint is represented by a primitive irreducible integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval, and its algebraic degree is at most \(\max\{1,D-1\}\).
statements.justification: Completeness and an input-based size bound prevent the grammar from achieving soundness by refusing hard legal instances or hiding exponential proof objects.
statements.gap: Exact root-isolation papers bound algebraic certificates for supplied polynomials, but the polynomial-size composition with value links, tie handling, and relational model tables is not supplied by the causal or verification literature.
statements.consumer: A traffic-bound producer can always emit a finite replayable record whose checking cost is controlled by the explicit instance rather than by trust in neural or numerical optimization.

statements.statement: For the complete explicit three-copy relational forest instance with \(F(q)=\tfrac14+\tfrac12q-\tfrac13q^3\), there are source-reproducing endpoint groundings \(Z\) and a certificate \(Gamma\) with \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)=1\), certifying \(Theta=[\tfrac14,\tfrac14+\tfrac{\sqrt2}{6}]\) and \(qplus=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\). The checker rejects either a record selecting \(\tfrac14-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{6}\) or a record omitting the positive critical point.
statements.justification: The cubic simultaneously tests an interior optimizer, an irrational endpoint, an extraneous conjugate, and exhaustive critical-point accounting.
statements.gap: General algebraic procedures can verify the scalar identities, but no published relational certificate transaction includes the source-reproducing endpoint models.
statements.consumer: This is the bounded implementation gate before applying the grammar to larger relational traffic groundings.

statements.statement: For every supported-row vector \(eta\in Cn\) and every \(q\in[0,1]\), \(|H(eta,q)-H(etahat,q)|\le\delta\). Consequently, \(\Pr(\{H(eta0,q):q\in[0,1]\}\subseteq Kn)\ge 1-\alpha\). The reported \(Kn\) is a conservative confidence enclosure and is not asserted to equal the exact projection \(\bigcup_{eta\in Cn}H(eta,[0,1])\).
statements.justification: This separates structural nonidentification from sampling uncertainty while respecting repeated uses of each shared row.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. optimize over general confidence constraints; no surveyed RSCM result supplies the labeled occurrence-coupling radius for a shared row used repeatedly in one target grounding.
statements.consumer: The N3 traffic point can be reported with both its exact population support range and a finite-sample outer enclosure for noisy supported rows.

statements.statement: Under a supplied tree decomposition of width \(w\) for the intervened target ground graph and fixed finite alphabets, can the proof-carrying compilation handle produce the correct dense \(F\), all target-relevant context-incidence counts, and a locally checkable derivation in time and certificate length polynomial in the explicit grounding size and exponential only in \(w\), so that composition with \(Check\) certifies the sharp interval end to end?
statements.justification: The fixed checker consumes explicit assignment-level incidence and factorization records; a width-sensitive producer would remove that representation boundary without making a false unrestricted polynomial-time claim.
statements.gap: Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein give polynomial univariate model checking after explicit-state construction, while no identified paper controls compilation from a succinct relational grounding with context sharing.
statements.consumer: Bounded-treewidth traffic and object-interaction scenes could receive a single end-to-end certificate rather than an externally promised polynomial.

sampling_model.design: Independent repeated complete scenes from prespecified source skeletons; one representative node per supported type--context row is fixed before sampling.
sampling_model.units: Finite source scenes with the relational skeletons in \(Rsrc\).
sampling_model.treatment: The target intervention \(\operatorname{do}(a)\) is fixed; inferential randomness comes from sampled source scenes, not from target intervention assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Population transfer uses only positive source parent contexts for target-relevant rows other than \(rstar\). For confidence boxes, each prespecified representative source-node parent context is separately required to have positive probability; \(rstar\) remains unrestricted on \([0,1]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the prespecified positive-probability representative contexts, construct simultaneous rational coordinate boxes for supported categorical rows, intersect them with row simplices, choose rational \(etahat\), and use the labeled occurrence radius \(\delta\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The complete relational identification procedure returns an identifying expression or \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), and neural extrema agree exactly when the query is identified.
Canonical finite SCMs reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual sharp bounds to a polynomial program.
Polynomial programming yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds and confidence-region relaxations for discrete causal queries.
Untrusted algebraic root certificates can be checked skeptically by verified univariate CAD and Sturm--Tarski computations.
Root counting and interval subdivision decide univariate polynomial relation systems soundly and completely in PVS.
Exact real-root isolation with multiplicities and nonsquare-free inputs has explicit polynomial bit-complexity bounds.
Unnested univariate parametric Markov-chain model checking is polynomial-time after the parametric model is explicit.
A response-signature LP gives tight causal-order bounds and constructs attaining SCMs.

tldr: A finite Markovian relational SCM with exactly one target-relevant binary row unsupported by positive source parent contexts has a sharp interventional range equal to the exact image of one rational polynomial. A fixed skeptical certificate binds the complete schema, graphs, source tables, target query, context incidence, dense polynomial, and serialized endpoint groundings; its checker replays the relational target factorization before certifying exhaustive derivative roots, exact algebraic endpoints, and source-compatible finite-noise endpoint RSCMs, with size and checking cost polynomial in the complete explicit encoding. The interval strictly refines Ejaz and Bareinboim only when their complete procedure actually returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and \(F\) is nonconstant; a constant \(F\) gives the same point-identification conclusion. Supported-row confidence boxes use a separate sampling-positivity condition and yield a conservative occurrence-coupled enclosure. The first open extension is width-sensitive proof-carrying production from succinct groundings.

project_justification.gap: When the complete relational identification procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), it does not report the exact compatible causal range; general discrete-SCM bounding and univariate algebra do not jointly certify the relational derivation of the objective, source reproduction, algebraic extrema, and endpoint models.
project_justification.niche: Exactly one unsupported binary row collapses a high-dimensional causal program to a one-dimensional polynomial image without making endpoint attainment or causal certificate semantics automatic.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp image theorem, serializes common finite-noise endpoint RSCMs, and supplies a sound, complete certificate that binds and replays the complete fixed relational instance with polynomial size and checking cost, followed by an explicitly conservative sampling enclosure under separately stated representative-context positivity.

related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim define RSCMs, give the relevant target-context support result, and supply a complete identification procedure with a neural criterion. The only strict comparator promise is conditional: when that complete procedure actually returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and \(F\) is nonconstant, the sharp interval is more informative; a missing sufficient support condition alone is not treated as failure, and constant \(F\) yields equal point identification. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide the canonical finite-SCM equivalence and sharp polynomial-program construction that informs the causal completeness argument. Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxation; the present exact univariate solver and occurrence-coupling enclosure are different specializations, not claimed improvements to their general algorithm. Kline and Tamer's 2023 review supplies the current partial-identification framing of identified-set characterization and set coverage. Li, Passmore, and Paulson supply the skeptical producer--checker architecture, while Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply sound root-counting and multiplicity-aware isolation primitives. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein show that explicit univariate parametric model checking is polynomial for unnested formulas, which marks the occupied algebraic core and motivates width-sensitive production from succinct groundings. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining SCMs for order-based LP bounds over a broader nonrelational class; their witnesses do not enforce the present type-shared independent-ground-noise semantics.
technical_internal_limitation: The fixed certificate transaction includes the complete explicit relational instance, context incidence, dense coefficient list, and a replayable target-factorization derivation. Producing this explicit input from a succinct relational description by exhaustive target-assignment expansion may be exponential. The confidence result does not compute the exact multivariate projection over supported-row boxes; interior nuisance optima and a maximum-clique encoding rule out a generic vertex-enumeration shortcut.
honest_scope: The interval identity and breakpoint witness architecture are mathematically concrete but remain to be proved in the typed core. The load-bearing work is the universal soundness, completeness, size, and checking theorem for a grammar that binds the complete fixed relational instance, verifies membership in \(Mone\), and replays the factorization yielding \(F\), followed by the independent cubic producer--checker transaction. General succinct compilation, several unsupported rows, conditional postintervention queries, efficient confidence width, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. Failure of a sufficient support condition does not itself imply that the complete Ejaz--Bareinboim procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\). As sanity reductions, \(F(q)=q\) gives the logical range \([0,1]\), while constant \(F\) gives a singleton and agrees with point identification.

seed_details.seed: A fixed skeptical certificate grammar for exact one-unseen-row relational causal bounds
seed_details.anchor: EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Theorem 4.3, Theorem 5.2, Corollary D.6, Section 6.1, and Appendix E.3--E.4; LiPassmorePaulson2019UnivariateCertificates, Sections 3--5
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first unresolved step is no longer root isolation alone: it is the compositional theorem that a digest-bound replay of the complete explicit relational instance, factorization, exhaustive derivative roots, algebraic value links, ties, and serialized endpoint groundings implies the global causal sharp-set claim.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to the skeptical univariate procedure of Li, Passmore, and Paulson, the first changed step is to validate the full schema, graphs, source tables, query, assignment-level context incidence, and model groundings, and to replay the derivation of the checked polynomial before applying univariate checks.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for relational SCM certificate, exact algebraic causal bound certificate, and one-parameter reachability certificate found univariate proof procedures and parametric model checking, but no certificate language joining those algebraic clauses to relational-source reproduction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from univariate CAD because the target is a polynomial in one variable. Rebuttal: CAD certifies a polynomial assertion but does not certify the relational derivation of that polynomial, shared-row legality, source reproduction, or attaining common endpoint SCMs; those semantic clauses are the kernel.

seed_details.seed: A sharp polynomial-image theorem with common finite-noise endpoint relational SCMs
seed_details.anchor: EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Theorem 4.3 and Section 6.1; ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF, Theorems 2.4 and 2.8
seed_details.proof_boundary: The support theorem fixes supported rows but does not characterize the continuum of target values when exactly one type-shared row is absent. The missing direction constructs, for every \(q\in[0,1]\), one finite-noise RSCM that preserves every source law.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to canonical-SCM polynomial programming, the first changed step eliminates every response-function coordinate except a single shared conditional row and proves that repeated target occurrences must use the same scalar \(q\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for relational partial identification, unsupported relational context bounds, and shared conditional-row polynomial images found general polynomial programs and causal-order LP bounds, but no exact one-row relational image theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: tightness follows immediately by optimizing the canonical polynomial program. Rebuttal: the unrestricted canonical feasible set can untie repeated occurrences; the required common inverse-CDF construction is what proves attainability inside the type-shared independent-ground-noise class.

seed_details.seed: A conservative occurrence-coupling confidence enclosure for sampled supported rows
seed_details.anchor: DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds, Section 7 and Appendix C; EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Experiment 6.1
seed_details.proof_boundary: The source confidence event concerns shared conditional rows, whereas the target grounding may reuse one uncertain row several times. The missing proof couples target systems in topological order and counts labeled occurrences rather than distinct rows.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to Autobounds, the first changed step is to replace exact optimization over a confidence region by a uniform total-variation perturbation lemma \(\delta=\min\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\}\) that remains valid under repeated relational use.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for repeated relational mechanism uncertainty, confidence bounds for shared conditional tables, and set-identified relational inference found multinomial regions and general set-inference inversion, but not the labeled occurrence-coupling layer.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is only a union bound around existing confidence boxes. Rebuttal: the substantive step is a pathwise coupling through an acyclic relational grounding with adaptively realized contexts; counting each row once is false, and exact nuisance projection is deliberately not claimed.

seed_details.seed: Exact fixed-\(k\) semialgebraic sharp ranges for several unsupported shared rows
seed_details.proof_boundary: For \(k>1\), the first failed step is enumeration of roots of \(F'\): extrema may lie on cube faces or positive-dimensional critical loci, so exact elimination and global nonnegativity certificates must replace univariate ordering.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The destination target--method pair is fixed-dimensional relational polynomial optimization with exact elimination and SCM witnesses.
seed_details.destination_search: The scan found general polynomial programs, spatial branch-and-bound, and exact positivity certificates, but no fixed-\(k\) relational theorem with endpoint-model serialization and output-sensitive bounds.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: fixed-dimensional real algebraic geometry already gives the algorithm. Rebuttal: the algebraic image theorem is occupied, while relational witness semantics and explicit output accounting are not; nevertheless the causal increment is too diffuse for this first version.

seed_details.seed: A minimal algebraic-noise theorem for irrational sharp endpoints
seed_details.proof_boundary: Canonical finite SCMs establish finite support but do not quantify which noise masses must be algebraic when rational source laws have an irrational optimizer.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The first changed step is to sort every rational cumulative threshold against one selected algebraic optimizer and prove that only the split atom contributes two nonrational masses.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for algebraic noise SCM witnesses and irrational sharp causal bounds found no direct match.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: inverse-CDF thresholding makes the two-mass result bookkeeping. Rebuttal: it is a useful output theorem but not a sufficient standalone kernel, so it is retained only as a lemma in the selected package.

seed_details.proof_boundary: The one-row polynomial uses the diagonal \(q_1=\cdots=q_m\), whereas generic canonical relaxations optimize over the whole cube. The proposed frontier would characterize exactly when diagonal and cube extrema agree.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The destination target--method pair changes from univariate root isolation to diagonal-versus-multilinear-cube extremum equivalence.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for diagonal restriction extrema of multilinear polynomials and shared-parameter Markov chains found adjacent algebraic optimization but no relational iff theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: equality can be checked by running both optimizations. Rebuttal: a structural iff condition in coefficients or occurrence hypergraphs would be new, but no sufficiently simple condition emerged in the bounded scan.

seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed checker starts from an explicit assignment-level incidence table and replay trace. seed_details.proof_boundary: Under the one-row reduction, identification holds exactly when all nonconstant coefficients vanish.

literature_map.thread: Relational support and the traffic consumer
literature_map.settled: Theorem 4.3 transfers a supported unconfounded conditional across skeletons; Theorem 5.2 and Corollary D.6 justify complete identification and neural min--max testing; Section 6.1 documents an N3 car context missing from source A and an empirical max--min gap.
literature_map.unsettled: On fixed instances where the complete procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), the paper does not return the sharp compatible range, algebraic endpoints, or independently checkable relational SCM witnesses. A violation of the sufficient support condition alone is not equated with \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).

literature_map.thread: Canonical finite SCMs and general sharp polynomial programs
literature_map.settled: Canonical response functions make discrete counterfactual bounding finite and sharp; general objectives and constraints become polynomial programs, while weaker causal-order information can yield an LP with attaining SCMs.
literature_map.unsettled: None of these results exploits one type-shared unsupported relational row to obtain the exact image \(F([0,1])\), link each algebraic endpoint to a common source-reproducing RSCM, or provide the proposed composed certificate grammar.

literature_map.settled: Root isolation, multiplicity handling, Sturm--Tarski sign determination, and sound and complete checking of univariate polynomial relations are established with exact arithmetic and polynomial bit bounds for integer inputs.
literature_map.unsettled: These procedures accept polynomial propositions; they do not validate a relational grounding, source-table reproduction, shared-row semantics, candidate-to-value links, or finite-noise causal endpoint witnesses as one proof object.

literature_map.settled: For a univariate parametric Markov chain and unnested PCTL with expectation and comparison operators, existence of an admissible valuation is decidable in polynomial time after rational-function construction.
literature_map.unsettled: The explicit-state reduction may be exponential in a relational grounding and carries no causal source-compatibility or endpoint-model certificate.

literature_map.settled: Jointly covering regions for observed probabilities can be relaxed into conservative confidence bounds for a sharp causal set; multinomial confidence regions and set-coverage language are available. Kline and Tamer's recent review confirms that identified-set characterization and the distinction between parameter coverage and set coverage remain the standard organizing framework.
literature_map.unsettled: Repeated uses of a type-shared row require a relational perturbation argument. Exact projection over all supported-row boxes is neither supplied nor claimed here.

novelty_justification: The closest causal result is Ejaz and Bareinboim's complete relational identification procedure and neural extrema criterion. The strict relation is limited to fixed instances on which that procedure actually returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and \(F\) is nonconstant: the proposed theorem returns the full compatible interval and source-reproducing endpoint RSCMs. A support-condition violation alone is not used to infer failure, and constant \(F\) gives equal point identification. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim and Duarte et al. already establish general sharp polynomial-program representations, so univariate optimization itself is not claimed as new. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris already supply the root and sign machinery. The new theorem-level object is the composed causal certificate: a fixed grammar and checker whose accepted record binds the complete schema, graphs, source tables, target query, context incidence, polynomial, and serialized groundings; replays the relational factorization yielding \(F\); verifies membership in \(Mone\); certifies exhaustive feasible critical points and exact endpoint ordering including ties; and has size and checking bounds measured against the complete explicit input encoding. The statistical rung uses positivity only for prespecified representative conditioning contexts and is deliberately an outer confidence enclosure obtained by labeled occurrence coupling, not an exact multivariate projection.
